report.incidentSummary: Starting at 14:35:00 UTC (20:05 IST) on 2026-09-16, the assistant chat service suffered severe latency degradation (p95 jumping from ~7s to 24-26s) and occasional answer failures. The degradation was caused by the upstream LLM provider throttling assistant-orchestrator requests with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests ('quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500'). Assistant-orchestrator's traffic volume (~34.4 req/s, or ~2,065 req/min) exceeded this quota, triggering automated retry backoff loops of up to 3 attempts with 2-8s backoffs. These sequential backoffs pushed response times to 15-31 seconds, and requests exhausting all retries failed with fallback messages. Prompt update CHG-48222, suspected by the reporter, was deployed at 14:42 UTC (7 minutes after onset) and was ruled out as the cause.
report.rootCauseStatement: Assistant-orchestrator inbound request rate during peak hours reached ~34.4 req/s (~2,065 req/min), exceeding the upstream llm-provider quota of 1,500 requests per minute. Starting at 14:35 UTC, llm-provider returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, causing assistant-orchestrator to enter sequential retry backoff loops (2-8s delays over up to 3 attempts). This inflated end-to-end conversation durations to 20-30 seconds and caused answer failures when retries were exhausted.

hypotheses.cause: Assistant-orchestrator request volume (~2,065 req/min) exceeded the external LLM provider quota (limit=1500 requests per minute), triggering HTTP 429 Too Many Requests and orchestrator retry backoff loops of up to 3 attempts with 2-8s delays, inflating latency to 20-30s and failing upon retry exhaustion.
hypotheses.rationale: Inbound request rate to assistant-orchestrator was sustained at ~34.4 req/s (~2,065 RPM), exceeding the 1,500 RPM quota. Logs at 14:35 UTC confirm HTTP 429 responses with 'quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500', driving rate-limited counts to 40-60/min and retry counts to 37-53/min. Backoff delays of 2-8s across up to 3 attempts directly match the observed 20-30s latency and fallback errors.

hypotheses.cause: External llm-provider experienced upstream capacity degradation or unexpected quota clampdown to 1500 RPM during regional peak hours.
hypotheses.rationale: Client request volume was already ~2,065 RPM prior to 14:35 UTC without rate limiting, suggesting provider-side quota enforcement began or tightened around 14:35 UTC. However, the orchestrator traffic legitimately exceeded the contracted 1,500 RPM threshold.

hypotheses.cause: Prompt template deployment (CHG-48222) increased context token size and processing time, causing LLM call timeouts and latency regression analogous to PIR-2007.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48222 completed deployment at 14:42 UTC (20:12 IST), seven minutes after the incident onset at 14:35 UTC (20:05 IST). Throttling logs at 14:35:07 UTC occurred on version 0.42.0 (pre-deployment). Furthermore, llm_tokens_per_min remained completely flat (~321k tokens/min), disproving token inflation.

facts.statement: assistant-orchestrator request_rate was steady between 32.74 and 36.02 req/s (mean 34.41 req/s, equivalent to ~2,065 req/min) across the entire window from 13:45 to 16:15 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count surged from ~0 count/min prior to 14:35 UTC to 22.54 count/min at 14:35 UTC and sustained between 39.04 and 59.94 count/min through 16:10 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator retry_count surged from 1-3 retries/min to 19.9 retries/min at 14:35 UTC and sustained between 37 and 53 retries/min thereafter.
assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms increased from ~7s (6.8-7.5s) to 13.5s at 14:35 UTC and remained between 23.8s and 26.0s through 16:10 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator llm_latency_p95_ms jumped from ~5.5s to 10.65s at 14:35 UTC and settled between 21s and 23.2s from 14:40 UTC onwards.

assistant-orchestrator logs starting at 14:35:07.794 UTC show recurring HTTP 429 Too Many Requests from llm-provider stating 'quota exceeded: requests per minute, limit=1500' on version 0.42.0, triggering retries with backoff delays of 2-8s over up to 3 attempts.
Conversations that exhausted all 3 retry attempts failed with fallback messages to the user.
assistant-orchestrator llm_tokens_per_min remained flat between 310k and 338k tokens/min throughout the entire window (mean ~321k tokens/min).
Deployment CHG-48222 on assistant-orchestrator (upgrading 0.42.0 to 0.43.0 with prompt template update) completed at 14:42:00 UTC, seven minutes after incident onset at 14:35 UTC.
user-context-service and portfolio-service showed normal latency (mean 196.3ms and 131.9ms respectively), baseline timeouts (<1.4/min), and normal cache hit rate (~93.7%).

inferences.statement: The 20-30s assistant latency observed by users was directly caused by sequential backoff retry loops (2-8s per attempt across up to 3 attempts) following 429 responses from llm-provider.

The prompt template update CHG-48222 was not the trigger of the latency spike or rate limiting, because symptoms began at 14:35 UTC under version 0.42.0, token consumption was unchanged, and CHG-48222 finished deploying at 14:42 UTC.
The service was generating ~2,065 conversations/min, which exceeds the provider rate limit of 1,500 requests/minute cited in the 429 error messages.

assumptions.statement: Each inbound conversation turn to assistant-orchestrator initiates at least one outbound request to llm-provider.

timeline.event: Assistant chat operating normally at ~34 req/s (~2,065 req/min) with p95 latency ~7s, rate_limited_count near zero, and 1-3 retries/min.

Incident onset: llm-provider begins rejecting calls with HTTP 429 (quota exceeded: limit=1500 RPM). Assistant-orchestrator p95 latency jumps to 13.5s, rate_limited_count rises to 22.5/min, and retry_count rises to 19.9/min.
Rate limiting intensifies: rate_limited_count reaches ~59/min, retry_count reaches ~40/min, and p95 latency jumps to 24.1s as requests accumulate backoff delays.
Deployment CHG-48222 completed for assistant-orchestrator (v0.42.0 -> v0.43.0); token rates remain unchanged (~321k tokens/min).
Repeated 429 errors cause retry exhaustion on multiple requests, resulting in fallback error messages sent to users.
Support duty manager reports incident INC-9062 (SEV2).

confidence.rationale: High confidence: Metrics and logs establish the exact chain of causation from provider HTTP 429 rate limiting (1500 RPM limit) to backoff retries and 24-26s p95 latency. Request rate queries proved that traffic volume was ~2,065 req/min, exceeding the quota. CHG-48222 was conclusively ruled out due to timestamp mismatch (14:42 UTC vs 14:35 UTC) and flat token metrics.

recommendedActions.rationale: Current baseline traffic of ~34.4 req/s (~2,065 req/min) breaches the hard provider cap of 1,500 req/min, causing continuous throttling.

recommendedActions.action: Implement client-side rate limiting or request queuing with token-bucket shedding at assistant-orchestrator ingress, rather than cascading retries into a throttled upstream provider.
recommendedActions.rationale: Retrying 3 times with exponential backoff on 429 responses exacerbates upstream rate limit breaches and forces user response times to 20-30 seconds.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate rate limiting in staging and ensure requests fail fast or queue cleanly without inflating p95 latency beyond acceptable thresholds.

recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents single-provider quota saturation or regional outages from degrading the core assistant product.
